labels.label: defi:ppcm

hypotheses.paper: M1, M2 singular flat spacetimes, M1∧M2 their greatest common sub-extension with φ : M1∧M2 → M2
hypotheses.note: any topological spaces X, Y, W and any maps j₁ : W → X, j₂ : W → Y; the definition itself needs nothing
the API (open embeddings of X, Y into the gluing, open projection, description of the generated equivalence) asks only that j₁, j₂ be open embeddings / injective

findings: ETT.tex:1990 the relation ∼ is not reflexive (p ∼ p only for p in the image of M1∧M2), so it is not an equivalence relation; the quotient is meant by the equivalence relation it generates, which is 'p = q or p ∼ q' when both maps are injective (Gluing.mk_eq_mk_iff). Suggest: 'the equivalence relation generated by …', or add 'p = q or'.

ETT.tex:1953-1960 (prop:Cauchy_pgcd, not this package): condition (b) of ℰ asks φ_M only to be a 𝕄≥0-morphism, not injective nor a Cauchy embedding, so (M1∧M2, φ) ∈ ℰ does not by itself make M1∧M2 a common sub-extension. defi:ppcm needs φ injective: if φ is not, M1 → M1∨M2 is not injective (Gluing.injective_j₂_of_injective_ι₁: ι₁ injective and j₁ injective force j₂ injective).

labels.label: rem:non_separe_cas

hypotheses.note: [T2Space X] [T2Space Y]; not used by t2Space_iff, C_eq_closure, disjoint_nhds_ι₁_ι₂_iff

hypotheses.paper: M0 globally hyperbolic, Cauchy surfaces Σ, Σ1, Σ2, second countability

findings: ETT.tex:2011 C is defined as the pairs (p,q) ∈ M1×M2 with π(p), π(q) not separated. Two equal points are never separated, so C contains every (j₁(x), j₂(x)) (Gluing.graph_subset_C) and C ≠ ∅ as soon as N ≠ ∅, even when the quotient is Hausdorff (Gluing.t2Space_and_C_nonempty). The last sentence of rem:non_separe_cas ('it is the case C ≠ ∅') is therefore false as written, and so is prop:Cauchy_point_min's hypothesis 'C ≠ ∅' in its literal reading. Every use of C (lem:corresponding_K, cor:model_corresponding, prop:C_connexe 'C is closed', prop:Cauchy_point_min, proof of prop:ppcm_Cauchy at l.2320-2324) needs the pairs with DISTINCT non-separated images. Suggest: add 'distinct' (or π(p) ≠ π(q)) to the definition of C. With that reading (Gluing.Cdist) the remark is proved: Cdist = closure(graph) ∖ graph ⊆ ∂j₁(N) × ∂j₂(N), and the quotient is Hausdorff iff Cdist = ∅.

The literal C is exactly the closure in M1×M2 of the graph {(j₁(x), j₂(x))} (Gluing.C_eq_closure, no separation axiom): this is the neighbourhood form of the sentence 'a sequence (a_n) with j₁(a_n) → p and j₂(a_n) → q exists because π(p) and π(q) are not separated' in the proof of lem:corresponding_K (l.2111). A cleaner statement of the whole remark: the gluing is Hausdorff iff M1, M2 are and the graph of f = j₂∘j₁⁻¹ is closed in M1×M2 (Gluing.t2Space_iff).

The remark is a necessary condition only: a pair in ∂j₁(N)×∂j₂(N) need not be non-separated; 'only the last case obstructs' is proved as: for Hausdorff M1, M2 the quotient is Hausdorff iff every pair of ∂j₁(N)×∂j₂(N) has separated images (Gluing.t2Space_iff_frontier). The line with two origins (two copies of ℝ glued along ℝ∖{0}) is the example: (0,0) ∈ Cdist and the gluing is not Hausdorff.
questions: Is C meant as the pairs with distinct non-separated images (equivalently, for Hausdorff M1, M2, C ⊆ ∂j₁(N) × ∂j₂(N))? Taken: yes, as Gluing.Cdist; the literal C is also formalized (Gluing.C) and shown to equal the closure of the graph.

kb_proposals: Gluing two spaces along open embeddings: CausalScaffold.Pushout (Causal.Gluing j₁ j₂ = Quot of the paper's relation); Hausdorff iff both pieces are and the graph is closed (Gluing.t2Space_iff); separation of ι₁ x, ι₂ y iff (x,y) ∉ closure graph (Gluing.disjoint_nhds_ι₁_ι₂_iff).

A causality on X transports along an open embedding e : X → Z to a LocalCausality on range e (Causality.pushLocal); two such on an open cover, compatible on overlaps, glue by Causality.generated (Gluing.causality is the worked example).
Quot.eqvGen_exact h then induction: clear h first (kb/0003 again); LocalCausality.extend_le_iff often needs (L := …) given explicitly, and Precausality.generated_le_iff needs (hU := …).
